name: Desolace
summary: Across Desolace, centaur tribes fight for the plains as Horde, Alliance, and demonic cults press into the wastes. Gray earth, storm-dark skies, ancient ruins, and fallen beasts mark Kalimdor’s western coast.

sections.title: A Land Cursed and Broken
sections.body: Storm-dark skies hang over Desolace, where gray earth lies broken and pools have turned yellow. Legend says Princess Theradras, an earth elemental, drained the land’s life to restore her form. Zaetar, son of Cenarius, came to subdue her, but became her mate instead. Their union brought the first centaur. Ashamed and enraged, the newborn centaur killed their father and spread across the plains, leaving the scarred waste travelers see today.

sections.title: Warring Hooves
sections.body: Thousands of hooves thunder across Desolace as four centaur tribes fight outsiders and one another. The Kolkar roam the eastern cliffs, while the Magram keep crude yurts around brackish sinkholes. Farther south, the Gelkis live beyond rope bridges in deep ravines. The fanatical Maraudine guard the approach to Maraudon. Travelers crossing the wastes are often drawn into this old blood feud. Safe passage may mean fighting one tribe to win a wary parley with another.

sections.title: Cults and Shadowed Coasts
sections.body:
Beyond centaur lands, dangers gather along Desolace’s borders. The Burning Blade operates from Thunder Axe Fortress and Shadowbreak Ravine, summoning demons and satyrs whose fel fire threatens the region.

Naga creep onto the storm-lashed beaches of Ethel Rethor, while Darkspear trolls spear fish from the stilts of Shadowprey Village. High in the northern crags, the Alliance keeps watch from Nijel's Point. They fear Horde expansion and the demonic taint spreading from Mannoroc Coven.

faq.q: Why is Desolace such a dead wasteland?
faq.answer: Legend says Desolace was once fertile, until Princess Theradras drained its vitality to rebuild her form. Then the centaur were born and spread violently, destroying what plant life remained and leaving gray dust and ash.

faq.q: Where did the centaur come from?
faq.answer: The centaur were born from Zaetar, son of Cenarius, and Princess Theradras, an earth elemental. Repulsed and enraged by their appearance, the first khans killed their father soon after birth and spread across the plains.

faq.q: Can I ally with the centaur tribes here?
faq.answer: Yes. You can earn standing with either the Gelkis or the Magram by slaying members of the rival tribe. Enough standing grants entry to that tribe’s village and peace within its territory, while the opposing tribe becomes permanently hostile.

Maraudon is the centaur’s sacred ancestral burial ground, hidden in Desolace’s twisting western cliffs. It holds Zaetar’s tomb and Princess Theradras’s underground lair, where she channels elemental corruption through its caverns.

faq.q: Who is the wanderer roaming Desolace with a bear?
aliases: who is the orc with a bear
faq.answer: The wanderer is Rexxar, Champion of the Horde, traveling with his loyal bear Misha. The half-ogre patrols the dusty roads of Desolace and the Stonetalon Mountains, watching the wilderness and aiding those on important Horde business.

faq.q: Why are the Alliance and Horde fighting the Burning Blade here?
faq.answer: The Burning Blade has seized strongholds such as Thunder Axe Fortress to summon demons and bind felsteeds. Its demons and satyrs threaten to infest the region, so both the Horde and Alliance must confront them.

angles.text: For tauren, Desolace is sacred and tragic ground: the centaur’s cradle, where their scourge drove your people close to extinction.

Desolace’s dry plains and demonic sites such as Mannoroc Coven draw warlocks seeking secrets of felsteeds. These wild horses were twisted into fire-breathing horrors by forbidden Shadow Council rites.
Cenarion Circle druids see Desolace as a terrible wound in nature, where Zaetar met his end and elemental decay chokes the earth.
From Nijel's Point, the Alliance watches the dangerous centaur tribes, Horde settlements such as Shadowprey Village, and demonic cults spreading through Desolace.

The Horde works to secure the coast at Shadowprey Village and protect the kodo herds at Ghost Walker Post. It also fights to crush the Burning Blade and prove the modern Horde has escaped demonic influence.
